title: The surah opens by swearing by the Day itself.
subtitle: Why the oath is by the very thing denied
then: This is one of the earliest surahs revealed in Makkah. People there said {trap}bodies would never be raised again.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains that the oath opens with a strong denial of their claim, then swears by the Day itself to {idea}affirm the final return.{/idea}
now: Death comes up at a funeral, and for a few minutes everyone is quiet. Then the drive home, the radio, the bills, the next week. The Day slides back into the fog of "someday." {idea}This verse pulls it out of the fog and names it.{/idea}
old: The Day of Resurrection is a far-off idea I will think about later.
new: It is so certain that it is sworn by, not just mentioned.
try: Say once today, slowly: there is a Day, and I will stand in it.

title: The voice inside that blames you is sworn by.
subtitle: The self-reproaching soul and why it matters
then: Al-Hasan Al-Basri said every believer blames himself: {idea}what did I mean by that word, by that meal, by that thought?{/idea} The sinner, he said, {trap}just carries on and never blames himself.{/trap} Mujahid added that this soul regrets the good it missed.
now: You snap at your child, and an hour later something inside you says, that was not fair. You scroll past a message from your mother and feel a small sting. {reward}That sting is not your enemy.{/reward} It is the part of you still awake.
old: That nagging voice after I mess up is something to shut off.
new: The soul that blames itself is alive, and Allah honors it with an oath.
try: Tonight, ask yourself one question: what did I intend by one thing I did today?

title: Scattered bones are not a problem for their Maker.
subtitle: The doubt about being put back together
then: Ibn Kathir explains the question: does man think Allah is not able to {idea}return his bones and gather them from their various places?{/idea} The doubters of Makkah looked at old graves and {trap}thought the matter was closed.{/trap}
now: You stand at a grave that is decades old. Nothing of the person seems left. It feels final, like a file deleted. {idea}The verse asks you to remember who made that person the first time.{/idea}
old: Once a body is gone to dust, that is the end of the story.
new: Dust is not out of reach for the One who made it into a person once.
try: Make a short dua for one person you have lost, by name.

title: Not just bones, even the fingertips.
subtitle: The finest detail is restored too

key.label: What He is able to do

then: The doubter asked about bones. The answer goes further: {idea}Allah is able to put together even the tips of his fingers in perfect order.{/idea} Ibn Kathir notes that if He willed, He could even make them all equal. {reward}His power is more than enough.{/reward}
now: Look at your hand on your phone screen. The tiny ridges on each fingertip, the joints that bend just right to type. {idea}The One who gave you that detail is not short of power to restore it.{/idea}
old: Bringing a person back would be too complicated to be real.
new: The smallest detail of me is already proof of how able He is.
try: Look at your fingertips for ten seconds and say SubhanAllah.

title: The real reason for doubt: he wants to keep going.
subtitle: Denial that serves a desire
then: Mujahid said this means man {trap}wants to push ahead following his own whims.{/trap} Ibn Abbas said it is the one who denies the Day of Reckoning. The verse names the motive: {idea}the doubt is not about bones, it is about freedom from account.{/idea}
now: You already know the thing you are doing is wrong. So you start reading articles that say it is fine, or that nobody really knows. {idea}Sometimes the argument is built to protect the habit.{/idea}
old: My doubts are purely intellectual.
new: Some of my doubts exist because I do not want to stop something.
try: Ask yourself honestly: is there one belief I hold mainly because it lets me off the hook?

title: When is it? asked by someone who means never.
subtitle: A question that is really a denial
then: Ibn Kathir says this question {trap}is only a question of denying its occurrence.{/trap} He links it to another verse where people asked when the promise would come, and were told {idea}it is a fixed Day that will not move by an hour.{/idea}
now: Someone in the group chat jokes: the world was supposed to end ten times already. Everyone laughs. It feels clever. {idea}The date was never the point. The point is the person asking.{/idea}
old: If no one can tell me when, I do not need to worry about it.
new: Not knowing when is exactly why I prepare now.
try: Replace one "when" question in your head with: what would I fix if it were soon?

title: The eyes that looked away will be dazzled.
subtitle: The first sign: sight overwhelmed
then: This answers the mocking question with a scene. Ibn Kathir says the eyes will be {trap}dazzled, humbled, and diminished{/trap}, looking here and there, unable to rest on anything. The one who asked "when" {idea}gets his answer in what he sees.{/idea}
now: You choose all day what your eyes rest on: the feed, the screen, the next video. Your sight feels like yours to steer. {idea}One day it will not be steered.{/idea} What it rests on now is still your choice.
old: My eyes are mine to point wherever I like.
new: The sight I use freely now will one day be overwhelmed. I should use it well.
try: Close one app today a little earlier than usual and look at something real.

title: The moon, so steady every night, loses its light.
subtitle: The most reliable light goes out
then: Ibn Kathir says simply that {trap}its light will go away.{/trap} The people of Makkah set their months by the moon. {idea}The thing they trusted most to come back each night will not.{/idea}
now: You check the moon on a clear night and it is just there, like it always is. Your routine, your job, your health feel the same way: always there. {idea}Even the moon has an end date.{/idea}
old: Some things in life are simply permanent.
new: Even the steadiest light is borrowed. Only its Maker stays.
try: Next time you see the moon, thank Allah for one steady thing you take for granted.

title: Sun and moon, never together, brought together.
subtitle: The order of the sky folded up
then: Mujahid said {trap}they will be rolled up.{/trap} Ibn Zayd linked this to the verses about the sun being wound round and the stars falling. {idea}The order that seemed to run by itself was always held by Allah.{/idea}
now: Sunrise times on your prayer app, the moon phases, the seasons. It all feels like a machine that runs itself. {idea}This verse reminds you there is a Hand on it.{/idea}
old: The universe runs on its own, like a clock no one wound.
new: The sky keeps its order because Allah holds it, and He will fold it.
try: At sunset today, pause for a moment and remember who keeps it on time.

title: The man who asked when now asks where to run.
subtitle: From mockery to panic
then: Ibn Kathir says man {trap}will see these horrors and want to flee{/trap}, asking where the escape or refuge is. The same voice that asked {idea}"when is the Day?" in verse 6{/idea} now only asks for a way out.
now: You ignore a growing problem: a debt, a lump, a strained marriage. It is easy to be calm while it is far away. Then one day it is in the room and all you want is an exit. {idea}The time to face it is while it is still far.{/idea}
old: I will deal with it when it actually comes.
new: When it comes, the only question left is where to run. Better to turn now.
try: Pick one thing you have been avoiding and take one first step on it today.

title: No hiding place, no shelter, no salvation that way.
subtitle: The answer to where to run
then: Ibn Masud, Ibn Abbas and others said: {trap}there will be no salvation.{/trap} Ibn Kathir compares it to the verse saying there will be no refuge that Day and no denying. {idea}There is simply no place outside Allah's reach.{/idea}
now: You have hiding places: the late night, the second account, the excuse you tell your family. They work, for now. {idea}The only real refuge was never away from Allah. It is toward Him.{/idea}
old: If I keep it hidden well enough, it stays hidden.
new: There is no hiding from Him, so the safe move is running to Him.
try: Say one quiet istighfar today for something no one else knows about.

title: Every road ends at your Lord.
subtitle: The final place of rest
then: After "there is no refuge," the verse gives the one place left. Ibn Kathir says it means {idea}the place of return and the final destination.{/idea} Notice it says {reward}your Lord{/reward}, addressed to the Prophet ﷺ: the One who raised and cared for you.
now: You plan everything: the career path, the house, retirement. All of it is a stop on the way. {idea}The address at the end of the trip is already written.{/idea} The question is how you arrive.
old: My life is heading wherever I steer it.
new: Wherever I steer, the last stop is my Lord. I want to arrive well.
try: Write one line in your notes: where I am really going. Read it before sleep.

title: What you sent ahead and what you held back.
subtitle: The full record, first to last

row.title: everything
sub: old and recent, small and large

then: Ibn Kathir says man will be informed of {idea}all of his deeds, the first and the last, the small and the large.{/idea} He connects it to the verse where people {trap}find everything they did placed before them{/trap}, and no one is wronged.
now: Your phone has a screen-time report. Your bank has a statement. You rarely open them because you do not want to see the totals. {idea}One report will be read to you in full.{/idea} You can still add to the good side.
old: Most of what I do is too small to count.
new: Small and large are both written. So small good is worth doing.
try: Do one small hidden good today that you would be glad to find on your record.

title: You already know yourself better than any witness.
subtitle: Man as a witness against himself
then: Ibn Abbas said the witnesses are {idea}his hearing, his sight, his hands, his legs, his limbs.{/idea} Qatadah said you see this person {trap}noticing other people's sins while blind to his own.{/trap}
now: You can list your colleague's flaws in a minute. Your sibling's too. Ask you about your own, and you go quiet, or change the subject. {idea}You know. You have always known.{/idea}
old: Other people's faults are more obvious than mine.
new: I am the best witness to my own faults. I should start there.
try: Before you think about anyone else's fault today, name one of your own.

title: Excuses will be offered. They will not change the facts.
subtitle: Arguing against what you already know
then: Mujahid said even if he {trap}argues in his own defense, he is a witness against it.{/trap} Ibn Abbas cited the verse that {idea}excuses will not profit the wrongdoers that Day.{/idea} Some will even swear they never did wrong.
now: You have a polished story ready for every slip: traffic, stress, they started it. It works on your boss and your spouse. {idea}Excuses that work here are practice for a court where they will not.{/idea}
old: With a good enough explanation, I am off the hook.
new: Excuses do not erase what I did. Owning it now is what helps.
try: Next time you slip today, skip the excuse and just say: I was wrong.

title: Do not rush to grab it. Just listen.
subtitle: A pause in the surah to teach how to receive
then: The surah stops mid-theme. Ibn Abbas described how the Prophet ﷺ {trap}struggled hard to grasp the revelation and moved his lips rapidly{/trap} while Jibril recited. Revelation was still new to him. Allah told him: {idea}do not move your tongue to hasten it.{/idea}
now: Someone is talking to you and you are already typing notes, or forming your reply, so you will not lose anything. You catch the words and miss the meaning. {idea}Sometimes holding on tight is the reason it slips.{/idea}
old: If I do not grab it fast, I will lose it.
new: Some things are kept for me when I stop clutching and simply listen.
try: In your next conversation, listen to one full answer before you think of your reply.

title: Keeping it safe is Our job, not yours.
subtitle: Allah takes on gathering and recitation
then: Ibn Abbas explained: {idea}He will collect it in his chest so he can recite it.{/idea} Ibn Kathir calls this the first phase, gathering it in the heart. {reward}The weight of remembering was lifted from the Prophet ﷺ.{/reward}
now: You try to memorize a surah and panic that it keeps slipping. You think it all depends on your brain. {idea}You do the showing up. The keeping is from Allah.{/idea} Ask Him for it.
old: Learning Quran depends on how good my memory is.
new: I bring the effort. Allah is the one who places it in the heart.
try: Before your next Quran session, ask Allah to keep it in your heart for you.

title: When it is recited, follow along after.
subtitle: Listen first, then recite
then: Al-Bukhari's wording: {idea}whenever Jibril came, he would be silent, and when Jibril left he would recite it{/idea} just as Allah had promised. {reward}The promise held exactly.{/reward}
now: Your teacher reads a line and you jump in before they finish. Or you play a recitation while doing three other things. {idea}The Prophet ﷺ was taught to give it his whole silence first.{/idea}
old: I can listen and do something else at the same time.
new: Real learning starts with full, quiet listening.
try: Listen to one short surah today with nothing else running, then recite it once.

title: And explaining its meaning is also on Us.
subtitle: The third phase: clarity
then: Ibn Kathir lists three phases: {idea}gathering it in his chest, reciting it, then its explanation.{/idea} After memorizing, Allah would {reward}explain it and inspire him with its meaning as He intended.{/reward}
now: You read a verse and it does not make sense. You feel shut out, or you invent a meaning that fits your mood. {idea}Meaning is something Allah gives.{/idea} Asking Him, and learning from those who studied, is part of the path.
old: If I do not understand a verse right away, it is not for me.
new: Understanding is a gift Allah sends in stages. I can ask for it.
try: Pick one verse you do not understand and read its explanation today.

title: The real problem: you love what is right now.
subtitle: Back to the theme, with the root cause
then: The surah returns to its theme. Ibn Kathir says {trap}the only thing that made them reject the Day is that their only concern was this worldly life.{/trap} The word for it means {idea}the hasty, the immediate.{/idea}
now: The thing you can have tonight always beats the thing promised later. The show over the prayer. The sale over the savings. {idea}Not because you thought it through. Because it is closer.{/idea}
old: I would care more about the Hereafter if it felt more real.
new: It feels less real because I keep choosing what is right in front of me.
try: Notice one moment today where now beat later, and choose later once.

title: And the Hereafter is simply left aside.
subtitle: Neglect, not argument
then: Ibn Kathir says they were {trap}preoccupied and distracted from the Hereafter.{/trap} The verse does not say they disproved it. {idea}It says they left it.{/idea}
now: No one decides to stop praying. It is one missed prayer on a busy day, then a week. The Quran on the shelf is not rejected, just left. {idea}Neglect does the work quietly.{/idea}
old: I have not rejected anything. I am just busy.
new: Leaving it aside every day ends up in the same place as rejecting it.
try: Pick up one thing you have quietly left, a dua, a page, a prayer, and do it once today.

title: Some faces that Day will be glowing.
subtitle: Radiant faces, delighted with good
then: Right after naming those who love the immediate, the scene turns. Ibn Kathir says the word means {reward}splendid, radiant, glowing, delighted with goodness.{/reward} These are {idea}those who did not leave the Hereafter aside.{/idea}
now: You spend money and time on how your face looks: skincare, filters, the right angle. A face can glow for a photo. {reward}This glow is earned by quiet choices no camera saw.{/reward}
old: A bright face is about looks and good genes.
new: The face that will shine that Day is built by what I choose now.
try: Do one good deed today purely for the face you will have that Day.

title: Looking at their Lord.
subtitle: The greatest gift of all
then: Ibn Kathir says {reward}they will see Him with their very eyes{/reward}, confirmed in authentic hadith. The Prophet ﷺ said: you will see your Lord as you see this full moon, {idea}so do not let yourselves be overcome in missing the prayer before sunrise and before sunset.{/idea}
now: Your alarm goes off for Fajr and the bed is warm. Asr comes in the middle of a meeting. {idea}The Prophet ﷺ tied seeing Allah to those two prayers.{/idea} That is the context for the next hard morning.
old: Paradise is mainly about the comforts in it.
new: The greatest thing there is not a place. It is looking at Him.
try: Guard tomorrow's Fajr or Asr with that hadith in mind.

title: Other faces that Day will be gloomy.
subtitle: The same Day, a different face
then: Qatadah said these faces are {trap}gloomy{/trap}; As-Suddi said {trap}their color will change.{/trap} Ibn Kathir puts it beside the verse about faces turning white and faces turning dark. {idea}Same Day, same crowd, two very different faces.{/idea}
now: Two people in the same office, same salary, same commute. One prays, one does not bother. From the outside nothing looks different. {idea}The difference is being written on a face you will wear later.{/idea}
old: We all end up the same way in the end.
new: The end splits into two faces, and I am choosing mine today.
try: Think of one habit that pushes you toward the gloomy face, and drop it for one day.

title: They sense the crushing blow coming.
subtitle: Certainty that comes too late
then: Ibn Kathir says "thinking" here means {trap}they will be certain{/trap} something terrible is coming. Mujahid called it a disaster. {idea}The certainty they refused in this life arrives all at once.{/idea}
now: You know the feeling the night before results: you did not study, and now you are sure how it will go. {idea}The surah gives you that certainty early, while you can still study.{/idea}
old: I will believe it when I see it.
new: Certainty that comes only when I see it comes too late to help.
try: Turn one worry about the Hereafter into one small deed today.

title: When the soul reaches the collarbones.
subtitle: Death, the moment denial ends
then: Ibn Kathir explains: at death, {trap}you are not able to deny what you were told{/trap}, because you see it with your own eyes. The surah moves from the Day of Resurrection to {idea}a day every listener will meet sooner: their own death.{/idea}
now: A hospital corridor. A machine beeping. Family whispering outside the room. All the debates you had about belief are not in that room. {idea}Only what is true is.{/idea}
old: Death is something I will think about when I am old.
new: Death is the moment every argument ends. I would rather settle mine before.
try: Ask Allah today for a good ending, in your own words.

title: Who can cure him? The room asks, and no one can.
subtitle: Searching for a healer at the end
then: Ibn Abbas said it means: {idea}who will recite healing prayers over him?{/idea} Abu Qilabah said: {trap}who is the doctor that can cure him?{/trap} The people around the dying man search, and nothing works.
now: Your family group chat lights up: anyone know a specialist? Anyone have a contact? Everyone is calling someone. {idea}One day the calls will not help, and only what you sent ahead will.{/idea}
old: With enough money and the right contacts, there is always a fix.
new: At the end, no contact can buy more time. The prep is now.
try: Visit or call one person who is sick this week.

title: He knows now: this is the parting.
subtitle: The certainty of leaving everything
then: After the search for a cure fails, the dying man {trap}is certain it is the time of separation.{/trap} Ibn Kathir describes this as the moment death's terrors are seen. {idea}What he doubted in health, he is sure of now.{/idea}
now: You hold your grandmother's hand in the last week. She stops asking about the house and the money. She asks who will visit. {idea}At the parting, people see clearly what mattered.{/idea}
old: I will always have more time with the people and things I love.
new: Every bond here has a parting. I want to use the time well.
try: Tell one person you love something you would regret not saying.

title: Leg wound around leg: hardship meets hardship.
subtitle: The last day here, the first day there
then: Ibn Abbas said it is {trap}the last day of this world and the first of the Hereafter: hardship meeting hardship{/trap}, {reward}except for whom Allah has mercy on.{/reward} Al-Hasan said it is the two shins bound together, the legs that once carried him now still.
now: You walk all day without a thought: to the bus, up the stairs, to the fridge. Your legs feel like they will always carry you. {idea}One day they will be still, and you will be carried.{/idea} Where are they taking you now?
old: My body will keep carrying me where I want to go.
new: My legs are on loan. I want them to have walked to good places.
try: Walk somewhere good today: the mosque, a visit, an errand for someone else.

title: That Day, the drive is toward your Lord.
subtitle: The soul is taken back
then: Ibn Kathir says this is {idea}the place of return and the destination.{/idea} He cites the verse where Allah's messengers take the soul and {idea}they are returned to Allah, their true Master.{/idea} Verse 12 said the same about the Day of Resurrection; here it is about every death.
now: People say "rest in peace" and "they are in a better place" without thinking. {idea}The surah says exactly where they went: to their Lord.{/idea} That is also where you are going.
old: Death is a full stop.
new: Death is a journey that ends in front of my Lord.
try: Say Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un once today and think about its meaning.

title: He did not believe, and he did not pray.
subtitle: No good inside, no good outside
then: Ibn Kathir says this is the man {trap}who denied the truth in his heart and turned away from acting on it.{/trap} So {trap}there is no good in him, inside or outside.{/trap} After the scene of death, the surah shows the life that led there.
now: You tell yourself your heart is fine, so the prayers can wait. Or you pray on autopilot while your heart is somewhere else. {idea}The verse pairs the two: belief inside, prayer outside.{/idea}
old: As long as my heart is good, the outward acts do not matter much.
new: Belief and prayer go together. Each keeps the other alive.
try: Pray your next prayer with one moment of real attention in it.

title: Instead, he called it a lie and turned away.
subtitle: The two steps of rejection
then: The verse mirrors the one before: {trap}not believing became denying; not praying became turning away.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says he denied in his heart and {trap}turned from acting on its way.{/trap}
now: Someone sends you a reminder. First you think: that is extreme. Then you mute the chat. {idea}Deny, then turn away. Two small moves that shape a whole life.{/idea}
old: Ignoring a reminder is harmless. I am not attacking anyone.
new: Turning away is a choice, and it follows close behind denial.
try: The next reminder you get today, read it fully instead of scrolling past.

title: Then he strutted home, pleased with himself.
subtitle: Arrogance after rejecting the truth
then: Ibn Abbas said it means {trap}arrogantly{/trap}; Qatadah said {trap}strutting.{/trap} Ibn Kathir links it to the verse about one who {trap}was joyful among his people, thinking he would never come back{/trap}, but {idea}his Lord was ever watching him.{/idea}
now: You win the argument in the family chat by being sharp, not by being right. You put the phone down feeling great. {idea}Feeling pleased with yourself is not the same as being right.{/idea}
old: If I walk away feeling good, I must have handled it well.
new: A proud walk after turning from the truth is the worst kind of win.
try: Think of one argument you won unfairly and send a softer message.

title: Woe to you, and woe.
subtitle: A warning that answers the strut
then: Ibn Abbas reported that {idea}the Prophet ﷺ said this to Abu Jahl, then Allah revealed it.{/idea} Qatadah said Abu Jahl replied that he was {trap}the mightiest man walking between Makkah's two mountains.{/trap}
now: You have a moment of power: the bigger title, the louder voice, the one everyone is afraid to correct. It feels like nothing can touch you. {idea}That is exactly the feeling this warning answers.{/idea}
old: When I am strong, warnings do not apply to me.
new: The stronger I feel, the more I need to hear warnings.
try: Ask someone you trust to tell you one thing you do that comes across as arrogant.

title: Then again: woe to you, and woe.
subtitle: A threat followed by a threat
then: Qatadah said: {trap}it is a threat followed by a threat, just as you hear it.{/trap} Ibn Kathir compares it to the line "eat and enjoy yourselves for a little." {idea}The repetition is there because the first was brushed off.{/idea}
now: The warning light in your car comes on. You ignore it. A week later it flashes and beeps. {idea}Repeated warnings are a mercy. They mean you still have time.{/idea}
old: If a warning repeats, it is just nagging.
new: A repeated warning is a second chance I have not used yet.
try: Name one warning you have heard more than once, from a doctor, a friend, your own heart, and act on it.

title: Do you think you will be left to drift?
subtitle: Not unguided here, not forgotten after

row.title: after death
sub: raised, not left in the grave

then: As-Suddi said it means {trap}not resurrected{/trap}; Mujahid and Ash-Shafi'i said {trap}not commanded and forbidden.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says the verse includes both: {idea}man is guided in this life and gathered back to Allah after it.{/idea}
now: Some days feel like drift: wake, work, scroll, sleep. Nothing seems to matter much. {idea}The verse says your days are not empty. They have instructions, and they have a return.{/idea}
old: My life is mine to drift through however I like.
new: My life has a purpose here and an account after. It matters.
try: Write down one thing you are sure Allah wants from you, and do a piece of it today.

title: You started as a tiny drop.
subtitle: The first creation as proof of the second
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}uses the beginning of creation as proof for its repetition.{/idea} Was man not {trap}a weak drop of a lowly fluid{/trap}? The doubter of resurrection is reminded of his own start.
now: You feel big: your degree, your car, your opinions. You argue about what Allah can and cannot do. {idea}You were once a drop no one could see.{/idea}
old: I am too complex to be made again from nothing.
new: I was made from almost nothing once. That is the proof.
try: When you feel proud today, remember the drop. Say Alhamdulillah.

title: Then a clot, then shaped and balanced.
subtitle: Each stage by His design
then: Ibn Kathir describes it: {idea}a clot, then a lump of flesh, then formed, and the soul was blown into him.{/idea} Then he became {reward}a complete creation with healthy limbs.{/reward}
now: Someone shares an ultrasound in the family chat. Everyone sends hearts. A few weeks ago there was nothing visible. {idea}Each stage is the same Hand that will raise you again.{/idea}
old: Growing in the womb is just a natural process.
new: Every stage was shaped by Allah. The same power brings me back.
try: Make dua today for someone expecting a child.

title: From one drop, male and female.
subtitle: The pairs, by His decree
then: Ibn Kathir says man became {idea}either a male or a female by the permission and decree of Allah.{/idea} The same small drop becomes two different kinds of people. {reward}It is all one Creator's work.{/reward}
now: A gender-reveal party: balloons, cake, the whole family filming. Everyone cheers for the surprise. {idea}It was never a surprise to Him.{/idea}
old: What I am was decided by chance.
new: What I am was decreed by Allah, from a single drop.
try: Thank Allah for one thing about how He made you that you usually overlook.

title: Is He not able to bring the dead to life?
subtitle: The question the surah ends on
then: Ibn Kathir: is not He who made {idea}this perfect creation from a weak drop able to repeat it?{/idea} A Companion said that whenever he recited this verse he would say {reward}"Glory to You, of course,"{/reward} and that he heard it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
now: You reach the end of a surah and close the app. The question hangs there, and you move on. {reward}The Companions answered it out loud.{/reward} The last verse asks you something. Answer.
old: Quran questions are rhetorical. I just read past them.
new: When the Quran asks me something, I can answer it.
try: Next time you recite this verse, say Subhanaka, bala: Glory to You, yes.
